source_text:
χωρὶς τούτου μηδὲν ὑμῖν πρεπέτω, ἐν ᾧ τὰ δεσμὰ περιφέρω, τοὺς πνευματικοὺς μαργαρίτας, ἐν οἷς γένοιτό μοι ἀναστῆναι τῆ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν, ἦς γένοιτό μοι ἀεὶ μέτοχον εἶναι, ἵνα ἐν κλήρῳ Ἐφεσίων εὑρεθῶ τῶν Χριστιανῶν, οἳ καὶ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις πάντοτε συνῄνεσαν ἐν δυνάμει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
Οἶδα, τίς εἰμι καὶ τίσιν γράφω. ἐγὼ κατάκριτος, ὑμεῖς ἠλεημένοι: ἐγὼ ὑπὸ κίνδυνον, ὑμεῖς ἐστηριγμένοι:
πάροδός ἐστε τῶν εἰς θεὸν ἀναιρουμένων, Παύλου συμμύσται τοῦ ἡγιασμένου. τοῦ μεμαρτυρημένου, ἀξιομακαρίστου, οὖ γένοιτό μοι ὑπὸ τὰ ἴχνη εὑρεθῆναι, ὅταν θεοῦ ἐπιτύχω, ὃς ἐν πάσῃ ἐπιστολῇ μνημονεύει ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Ephesus while being taken under guard to Rome, and here he speaks of his chains and of Paul's memory of the Ephesians.
pass_a_gloss: Apart from this [man] let nothing be fitting for you, in whom I carry around the bonds, the spiritual pearls, in which may it be for me to rise by your prayer, of which may it be for me always to be a partaker, so that in the lot of the Ephesians I may be found, of the Christians, who also with the apostles always agreed in the power of Jesus Christ. I know who I am and to whom I write. I [am] condemned, you [are] shown mercy; I [am] under danger, you [are] established. You are a passageway of those being killed for God, fellow-initiates of Paul, the sanctified one, the one who has been witnessed to, worthy of blessing, of whom may it be for me under the footprints to be found, when I attain God, who in every letter remembers you in Christ Jesus.

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of pearls as precious spiritual treasures, appositional to 'bonds'

choices.english: in the lot of the Ephesians
choices.why: Preserves the image of a share or portion among the Ephesian Christians
rejected: in the inheritance of the Ephesians
among the company of the Ephesians

choices.term: πάροδός ἐστε τῶν εἰς θεὸν ἀναιρουμένων
choices.english: You are a passageway of those being killed for God
choices.why: Keeps the spatial metaphor of a road or way through which martyrs pass
rejected: You are the road of those slain for God
You are a way-station for those being put to death for God

choices.why: Preserves the mystery-cult connotation of shared initiation into sacred things

choices.english: to be found under the footprints
choices.why: Keeps the literal spatial image of being found beneath Paul's footprints, i.e., following closely
rejected: to be found in his footsteps
to be found following his tracks

pass_b_english: Let nothing be fitting for you apart from this, in which I carry around my bonds, my chains, which are spiritual pearls. Through your prayer may I be granted to rise in them, and may I always share in that prayer, so that I may be found in the inheritance of the Ephesian Christians, who always agreed with the apostles in the power of Jesus Christ.
I know who I am and to whom I write. I am condemned; you have been shown mercy. I am under danger; you are established.

You are fellow-travelers with those being killed for God, fellow believers with Paul, who was sanctified, who bore witness, and who is worthy of blessing. May I be found in his footsteps when I attain God. In every letter he remembers you in Christ Jesus.

problems.quote: in him I carry around my bonds
problems.why: ἐν ᾧ refers to πρεπέτω context, not 'him'; means 'in which [nothing be fitting]'
problems.fix: in which I carry around my bonds
problems.ruling: ἐν ᾧ is a neuter relative pronoun referring to “μηδὲν ὑμῖν πρεπέτω”, not to a person; translation “in him” mis‑links the clause.

problems.why: Greek says “being taken away from God,” not “killed for God.”
problems.ruling: εἰς θεὸν ἀναιρουμένων means 'being removed/reconciled to God'; 'killed for God' mistranslates the phrase and misleads the reader.

edits.old: Apart from him, let nothing be fitting for you—in him I carry around my bonds
edits.new: Apart from him, let nothing be fitting for you—in which I carry around my bonds

edits.old: You are a passageway for those being killed for God
edits.new: You are a passageway for those being taken away from God

problems.quote: a passageway for those being taken away from God
problems.source_quote: πάροδός ἐστε τῶν εἰς θεὸν ἀναιρουμένων
problems.why: εἰς θεόν means 'to God'; ἀναιρουμένων means 'being taken up to God,' not 'taken away from.'
problems.fix: a passageway for those being taken up to God
problems.ruling: Greek phrase "εἰς θεὸν ἀναιρουμένων" means ‘being taken to God’, not ‘taken away from God’, reversing the sense.

problems.quote: Apart from him, let nothing be fitting for you
problems.why: Greek says “apart from this”, not “apart from him”.
problems.fix: Apart from this, let nothing be fitting for you
problems.ruling: τούτου is neuter 'this', not 'him'; mistranslates the demonstrative's referent.

edits.old: Apart from him, let nothing be fitting for you
edits.new: Apart from this, let nothing be fitting for you

edits.old: You are a passageway for those being taken away from God
edits.new: You are a passageway for those being taken up to God

problems.quote: You are a passageway for those being taken up to God
problems.source_quote: πάροδός ἐστε τῶν εἰς θεὸν ἀναιρουμένων
problems.why: Greek says “those being taken away from God”, not “taken up to God”, reversing the direction.
problems.fix: You are a passageway for those being taken away from God
problems.ruling: ἀναιρουμένων means 'taken away/removed'; εἰς θεόν with ἀναιρουμένων means 'removed to God' (martyrdom), not 'taken up to God'.

edits.old: You are a passageway for those being taken up to God
edits.new: You are a passageway for those being taken away from God

problems.quote: Apart from this, let nothing be fitting for you—in which I carry around my bonds
problems.why: The dash and 'in which' create a broken construction.
problems.fix: Reconstruct: 'Let nothing be fitting for you apart from this, in which I carry my bonds.'

problems.quote: I am scum for you, and I purify myself for you Ephesians
problems.why: 'Scum' is likely too negative; the Greek probably means 'expiation' or 'scapegoat.'

edits.old: Apart from this, let nothing be fitting for you—in which I carry around my bonds
edits.new: Let nothing be fitting for you apart from this, in which I carry around my bonds

edits.old: You are a passageway for those being taken away from God
edits.new: You are a passageway for those being killed for God

fixed: The second reported problem about 'scum' does not appear in the provided English text; no such wording exists in the passage, so no edit was made for it.

problems.quote: fellow-initiates with Paul, the sanctified one, the one who bore witness
problems.why: Reader may be unsure whether 'sanctified one' refers to Paul or another figure.
problems.fix: Clarify that Paul is meant throughout this clause.

problems.quote: You are a passageway for those being killed for God
problems.why: 'Passageway' is odd; likely means 'companions on the way' or 'fellow-travelers.'

edits.old: You are a passageway for those being killed for God, fellow-initiates with Paul, the sanctified one, the one who bore witness, worthy of blessing.
edits.new: You are fellow-travelers with those being killed for God, fellow-initiates with Paul—the sanctified one, the one who bore witness, worthy of blessing.

fixed: The speaker ambiguity is resolved by making Paul the clear referent of 'the sanctified one, the one who bore witness, worthy of blessing' through the dash and singular construction.
The mistranslation of 'passageway' is corrected to 'fellow-travelers,' which better reflects the Greek πάροδος in context as companions on the way.

problems.why: Two different renderings for companionship terms in same sentence; unclear if distinct.
problems.fix: Clarify these are parallel metaphors, not two different groups.

edits.old: You are fellow-travelers with those being killed for God, fellow-initiates with Paul,
edits.new: You are a passageway for those being killed for God, fellow-initiates with Paul,

fixed: The English 'fellow-travelers' obscures the source's distinct metaphor of being a passageway (πάροδός) for those being killed for God, which is not a companionship term but a spatial image. Restored 'passageway' to match the source and clarify the parallel metaphors.

problems.quote: You are a passageway for those being killed for God
problems.why: 'Passageway' is odd; likely means 'fellow-travelers' or 'companions on the road' of martyrdom.
problems.fix: Check Greek; likely 'fellow-travelers' or 'those who share the road'.

edits.old: You are a passageway for those being killed for God
edits.new: You are fellow-travelers with those being killed for God

fixed: Changed 'passageway' to 'fellow-travelers' to reflect the Greek πάροδος as companions on the road, not a passageway.

problems.why: 'Pearls' for chains/fetters is an odd metaphor; reader may think of literal pearls rather than his chains.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'my chains, which are spiritual pearls.'

edits.new: my chains, which are spiritual pearls

fixed: The source τοὺς πνευματικοὺς μαργαρίτας refers to the bonds (τὰ δεσμὰ) Ignatius carries, so clarifying 'my chains, which are spiritual pearls' is warranted.

polish.changed: I clarified the broken construction in the first paragraph by separating the prayer clause into its own sentence, made the antecedent of 'in them' explicit as the spiritual pearls, and smoothed the rhythm of the final sentence while preserving every claim and reference.

notes.quote: Apart from this, let nothing be fitting for you—in which I carry around my bonds
notes.why: The dash and 'in which' create a broken construction.
notes.fix: Reconstruct: 'Let nothing be fitting for you apart from this, in which I carry my bonds.'

notes.quote: I am scum for you, and I purify myself for you Ephesians
notes.why: 'Scum' is likely too negative; the Greek probably means 'expiation' or 'scapegoat.'

polish.changed: Clarified that 'the sanctified one' refers to Paul by keeping the phrase attached to his name, and rendered 'passageway' as 'fellow-travelers' to match the intended sense of companionship on the way.

notes.quote: fellow-initiates with Paul, the sanctified one, the one who bore witness
notes.why: Reader may be unsure whether 'sanctified one' refers to Paul or another figure.
notes.fix: Clarify that Paul is meant throughout this clause.

notes.quote: You are a passageway for those being killed for God
notes.why: 'Passageway' is odd; likely means 'companions on the way' or 'fellow-travelers.'

polish.changed: Clarified 'fellow-initiates' as 'fellow believers' to remove the obscure mystery-religion term while preserving the intended Christian meaning.

notes.why: Technical term from mystery religions; unexplained and obscure to modern readers.
notes.fix: Gloss as 'fellow-initiates' or 'co-initiates' with note on mystery-cult background.

notes.why: Mystery-religion term; reader may not know it means fellow-Christians here.
Mystery-cult term is misleading for Christian context; Greek 'mystai' here means initiated believers.

polish.changed: Clarified 'the lot' as 'the inheritance' to avoid the sense of random chance, and kept Paul's identity explicit by retaining his name in the final paragraph. Preserved all claims, quotations, and references exactly.

notes.quote: the sanctified one, the one who bore witness
notes.why: Refers to Paul, but never named; reader may not identify him.
notes.fix: Add note: 'the sanctified one...bore witness' refers to Paul.

notes.why: Metaphor for chains is unexpected; pearls suggest value, not suffering.
notes.fix: Note: chains become precious through spiritual significance.

notes.quote: the righteous one is his own accuser (Proverbs 18:17)
notes.why: LXX Proverbs 18:17 is 'a righteous man accuses himself at the beginning of his speech'; Hebrew is different.
notes.fix: Note LXX version differs from Hebrew.

notes.quote: the lot of the Ephesian Christians
notes.why: 'Lot' here means assigned portion or inheritance, not a random draw; reader may misread.
